questions.qtext:
Given:

Compute:

SELECT R.A, R.B, S.B, S.C, S.D
FROM R FULL OUTER JOIN S ON (R.A > S.B AND R.B = S.C)

Which of the following tuples of $R$ or $S$ is/are dangling (and therefore needs to be padded in the outer join)?
questions.solution:
Answer: B, D

Selected solution (score: 0)
Answer is option $\boxed{B,D}$

Outer join can be conditoinal or natural , in this case it is conditional.

Given Condition is ( $R.A>S.B$ AND $R.B=S.C$ )

1. $R(1,2)$: in $S$ none of $2,4$ and $6$ smaller than $1$. Hence its dangling tuple.

2. $R(3,4)$: only tuple $S(2,4,6)$ satisfy the given condition.

3. $R(5,6)$: only tuple $S(4,6,8)$ satify the given conditon.

$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
R.A & R.B & S.B & S.C & S.D \\
\hline
1 & 2 & \text{NULL} & \text{NULL} & \text{NULL} \\
3 & 4 & 2 & 4 & 6 \\
5 & 6 & 4 & 6 & 8 \\
\text{NULL} & \text{NULL} & 4 & 7 & 9 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$

$S(4,7,9)$ and $R(1,2)$ are dangling tuples.
Source solution 2 (score: 3)

questions.qtext:
Consider the following SQL query:

SELECT DISTINCT s1.sname, s1.age
FROM student s1, student s2
WHERE s1.age > s2.age

This query returns
A: The name and age of one of the oldest student(s)
B: The name and age of all of the oldest student(s)
C : The name and age of all of the youngest student(s)
D: The name and age of all students that are older than the youngest student(s)
questions.solution:
Answer: D

Selected solution (score: 1)

Answer is option $\boxed D$

The condition $s1.age>s2.age$ check for every $s1$ row there exists some $s2$ row where $s2.age$ is smaller. Only $s1$ with smallest age will not have entry in the output table.

questions.qtext:
Compute the result of the following query on the above table $Arc(x,y)$:

SELECT a1.x, a2.y, COUNT(*)
FROM Arc a1, Arc a2
WHERE a1.y = a2.x
GROUP BY a1.x, a2.y

The number of tuples in the output is?
questions.solution:
Answer: 1

Selected solution (score: 0)

Answer would be $\boxed{6}$

Given condition is $ \text{WHERE } a1.y = a2.x $ and we are also grouping based on $\text{GROUP BY} a1.x,a2.y$.

Lets do it tuple by tuple.

$a1(1,2)$ satisfy the given condition with $a2(2,3)$ only therefore count value will be $1$ against group $(1,3)$

Again we have $a1(1,2)$ count value will become $2$ against group $(1,3)$

$a1(2,3)$ satisfy the given condition with $a2(3,4)$ and $a2(3,4)$ count of group $(2,4)$ is $2$

$a1(3,4)$ matched with $a2(4,1)$ and $a2(4,2)$ count of group $(3,1)=3$ and group $(3,2)=1$

Again we have $a1(3,4)$ count of group will become $(3,1)=6$ and $(3,2)=2$

$a1(4,1)$ will match with $a2(1,2)$ so count of group $(4,2)=2$

we have $a1(4,1)$ 2 more time therefore count of group $(4,2)$ becomes $6$.

Now at last we have $a1(4,2)$ which matches with $a2(2,3)$ therefore count of group $(4,3)=1$

Here is the final output of the table.

\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline a1.x & a2.y & COUNT(*) \\ \hline 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 6 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ \hline \end{array}​​
